key_insight: In blunt traumatic brain injury, trauma-specific and neurologically oriented scores (RTS, GCS, MGAP) predicted early mortality better than general early-warning scores, but overall performance was only modest.
clinical_relevance: These tools may help early triage and resource prioritization in the first 24 hours after admission, but they should complement—not replace—clinical judgment.
method: Retrospective single-center cohort of 444 adults with blunt TBI in a tertiary ICU (Tehran, 2022–2025).
Compared GCS, RTS, MGAP, MEWS, and REMS for predicting death within 24 hours.
Evaluated discrimination with AUC, 95% CI via 1,000 bootstrap resamples, and pairwise AUC comparisons; optimal cutoffs used the Youden Index.
evidence_signal: RTS had the highest AUC (0.676), followed by GCS (0.669) and MGAP (0.657); MEWS and REMS performed lower, and all AUCs remained below 0.70.
watch_item: Because the study was retrospective and single-center with only modest discrimination, the results may not generalize well to other hospitals or populations.
paper_title: Comparative Performance of Clinical Scoring Systems for Early Mortality Prediction in Blunt Traumatic Brain Injury
